about: A measured claim shown so it cannot be doubted (film-language/sequences.json the_proof). One act per claim; each act: overhead (the shadows on the line) → the contrast insert (the same frame on the other days at the same Sun height) → on the line, long lens (the body enters the frame the stones make) → the window held → release along the line. Days, moments, bearings and scenes come from the site; the compiler fills the beats with takes from cameras.json. Script v3.1's dawn act (shots 8, 8c, 9, 9b, 10, 11) is this strategy by hand.

claims.about: each claim is one act; 'day' names a day in the site's days table; 'moment' the key instant (moments.json); 'bearing' the line's bearing name (site.json bearings) and which way the camera looks along it; 'contrast_days' the other days for the insert
claims.fields: overhead_span_min / push_span_min: minutes from the moment for those beats (after it for a rising body, before it for a setting one); window_camera: the window beat's overrides of locked_tele_window; ids: the shot ids to emit (so a compiled film can be diffed against script v3.1); voice: per slot, else the strategy's template; bearing_window: the claim's measured bearing window for check

list.proves: the first light of the solstice rises up the axis, inside the Great Trilithon's slot

voice.overhead: Seen from above, at sunrise on the longest day, every stone throws its shadow the same way — south-west, straight down the monument's axis.
voice.contrast: On any other morning, the shadows point elsewhere.
voice.on_the_line: Stand on that line and look back north-east. The first light of the solstice appears inside the slot of the Great Trilithon.
voice.window: From the centre, the Sun clears the horizon at a bearing of 49 degrees, beside the Heel Stone — and for a few minutes it sits framed inside one window of the sarsen circle.

list.proves: the same axis takes the midwinter sunset from the other side

voice.overhead: Six months on, the shadows turn round. In the low winter afternoon they run north-east, up the same axis.
voice.on_the_line: The axis works both ways. From the other side, the midwinter Sun goes down through the same slot.
voice.window: At the solstice the setting Sun sits within a tenth of a degree of the centre of the Great Trilithon's window.

voice.line: Stand on that line and look along it. {proves}.
